pairing.UID_note: Anonymized full/quarter series can have distinct study/frame UIDs. Pairing is proved by common patient folder/header, instance, physical grid and exact DICOM-NPY pixels.

access.visualization_count_note: Recorded event counts in this object precede visualization. Additional cache reads are reconstructed from saved query/match metadata and the reader code, one np.load per unique (slice,dose). The same allowlist guard stayed active through visualization.

visual_review_text_only.review_type: visual inspection of 16-query contact sheet; qualitative, not a radiologist annotation
observations: Several high-contrast contours and tissue boundaries retrieve the exact patch or similar coarse geometry across slices.
For S100 (32,48) and S200 (35,92), non-coordinate Top1 still has similar boundary layout; demeaned patch correlations are 0.877 and 0.825.
Flat/proxy-flat queries S100 (46,50), S200 (96,54) and S300 (89,29) have Top1 demeaned correlations 0.060, -0.082 and 0.062. High NSE cosine does not establish fine texture identity.
S100 tissue-boundary proxy (72,73) also has an incorrect Top1 with weak patch correlation; category labels are image-statistic proxies, not expert anatomical labels.
S300 small-scale proxy (80,46) retrieves a different slice with only moderate geometric agreement (demeaned correlation 0.399).

NSE is not a guaranteed fine-grained anatomical identity matcher. Mean-HU-only hard retrieval is much weaker, so the features are not explained by scalar mean HU alone, but density/coarse-layout dependence remains.
visual_review_text_only.reason: Cross-dose same-position consistency and coarse discrimination are strong without collapse; exact retrieval degrades substantially and some weak-texture/boundary queries are ambiguous.
